name: Vildagliptin/metformin
className: Combination of oral blood glucose lowering drugs: DPP-4 inhibitor + biguanide

src.q: Each film-coated tablet contains 50 mg of vildagliptin and 1000 mg of metformin hydrochloride (corresponding to 780 mg of metformin).
Each film-coated tablet contains 50 mg of vildagliptin and 850 mg of metformin hydrochloride (corresponding to 660 mg of metformin).

bnf.note: BNF/BNFC is only available in the UK; not accessed.

items.t: Adults with type 2 diabetes, with diet and exercise: inadequately controlled on metformin alone; already taking vildagliptin and metformin as separate tablets; or with other diabetes medicines, including insulin.

src.q: in patients who are inadequately controlled with metformin hydrochloride alone
in patients who are already being treated with the combination of vildagliptin and metformin hydrochloride, as separate tablets
in combination with other medicinal products for the treatment of diabetes, including insulin, when these do not provide adequate glycaemic control

items.t: If no suitable fixed-dose strength is available for the patient's renal function, use the individual medicines instead of the combination tablet.

src.q: If no adequate strength of Eucreas is available, individual monocomponents should be used instead of the fixed dose combination.

items.t: One tablet (50 mg/850 mg or 50 mg/1000 mg) twice daily, morning and evening; maximum vildagliptin 100 mg daily. On metformin alone: vildagliptin 50 mg twice daily plus the metformin dose already taken. Switching from separate tablets: start at current doses.
items.tag: Type 2 diabetes, adults (normal renal function, GFR ≥ 90 mL/min)

src.q: while not exceeding the maximum recommended daily dose of 100 mg vildagliptin
Eucreas may be initiated at either the 50 mg/850 mg or 50 mg/1000 mg tablet strength twice daily, one tablet in the morning and the other in the evening.
The starting dose of Eucreas should provide vildagliptin as 50 mg twice daily (100 mg total daily dose) plus the dose of metformin already being taken.

items.t: With metformin plus a sulphonylurea, or with insulin: vildagliptin 50 mg twice daily and a similar metformin dose. With a sulphonylurea, a lower sulphonylurea dose may be considered.

src.q: When Eucreas is used in combination with a sulphonylurea, a lower dose of the sulphonylurea may be considered to reduce the risk of hypoglycaemia.
The dose of Eucreas should provide vildagliptin dosed as 50 mg twice daily (100 mg total daily dose) and a dose of metformin similar to the dose already being taken.

items.t: Elderly (65 years and over): monitor renal function regularly.

src.q: elderly patients taking Eucreas should have their renal function monitored regularly

items.t: Not recommended under 18 years; safety and efficacy not established and no data.

src.q: Eucreas is not recommended for use in children and adolescents (< 18 years).

items.t: Hypersensitivity to vildagliptin, metformin or any excipient.

src.q: Contraindications - Hypersensitivity to the active substances or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1

items.t: Any acute metabolic acidosis (e.g. lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis); diabetic pre-coma; severe renal failure (GFR < 30 mL/min).

src.q: Any type of acute metabolic acidosis (such as lactic acidosis, diabetic ketoacidosis) - Diabetic pre-coma - Severe renal failure (GFR < 30 ml/min)

items.t: Acute conditions that may alter renal function: dehydration, severe infection, shock, intravascular iodinated contrast.

src.q: Acute conditions with the potential to alter renal function, such as: - dehydration, - severe infection, - shock, - intravascular administration of iodinated contrast agents

items.t: Acute or chronic disease that may cause tissue hypoxia: cardiac or respiratory failure, recent myocardial infarction, shock.

src.q: Acute or chronic disease which may cause tissue hypoxia, such as: - cardiac or respiratory failure, - recent myocardial infarction, - shock.

items.t: Hepatic impairment; acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism; breastfeeding.

src.q: Hepatic impairment (see sections 4.2, 4.4 and 4.8) - Acute alcohol intoxication, alcoholism - Breast-feeding (see section 4.6)

items.t: Not a substitute for insulin; should not be used in type 1 diabetes.

src.q: Eucreas is not a substitute for insulin in insulin-requiring patients and should not be used in patients with type 1 diabetes.

items.t: Lactic acidosis (very rare, serious): risk rises with acute worsening of renal function, cardiorespiratory illness or sepsis. Stop temporarily in dehydration. Start medicines that can acutely impair renal function (antihypertensives, diuretics, NSAIDs) with caution.

src.q: Lactic acidosis, a very rare but serious metabolic complication, most often occurs at acute worsening of renal function, or cardiorespiratory illness or sepsis.
In case of dehydration (severe diarrhoea or vomiting, fever or reduced fluid intake), metformin should be temporarily discontinued and contact with a health care professional is recommended.
Medicinal products that can acutely impair renal function (such as antihypertensives, diuretics and NSAIDs) should be initiated with caution in metformin-treated patients.

items.t: Iodinated contrast (intravascular): stop before or at the time of imaging; restart no sooner than 48 hours after, once renal function is re-checked and stable.

src.q: Metformin should be discontinued prior to or at the time of the imaging procedure and not restarted until at least 48 hours after, provided that renal function has been re-evaluated and found to be stable

items.t: Mitochondrial disease (MELAS, MIDD): metformin is not recommended; withdraw immediately if suggestive signs appear.

src.q: metformin is not recommended due to the risk of lactic acidosis exacerbation and neurologic complications which may lead to worsening of the disease

items.t: Hepatic: should not be used in hepatic impairment (including pre-treatment ALT or AST > 3 x ULN). Rare hepatic dysfunction (including hepatitis) with vildagliptin; check liver function before and during treatment.

src.q: Patients with hepatic impairment, including those with pre-treatment ALT or AST > 3x ULN, should not be treated with Eucreas
Rare cases of hepatic dysfunction (including hepatitis) have been reported with vildagliptin.

items.t: Skin: blistering and exfoliative lesions reported; monitor for skin disorders such as blistering or ulceration.

src.q: monitoring for skin disorders, such as blistering or ulceration, is recommended

items.t: Acute pancreatitis: inform patients of the symptoms; stop if suspected; do not restart if confirmed. Caution with a history of acute pancreatitis.

src.q: If pancreatitis is suspected, vildagliptin should be discontinued; if acute pancreatitis is confirmed, vildagliptin should not be restarted.
Caution should be exercised in patients with a history of acute pancreatitis.

items.t: Hypoglycaemia with a sulphonylurea: a lower sulphonylurea dose may be considered.

src.q: Patients receiving vildagliptin in combination with a sulphonylurea may be at risk for hypoglycaemia.

items.t: Surgery under general, spinal or epidural anaesthesia: stop metformin at the time of surgery; restart no earlier than 48 hours after surgery or return to oral nutrition, once renal function is re-checked and stable.

src.q: Metformin must be discontinued at the time of surgery under general, spinal or epidural anaesthesia.
Therapy may be restarted no earlier than 48 hours following surgery or resumption of oral nutrition and provided that renal function has been re-evaluated and found to be stable.

items.t: Alcohol: combination not recommended (lactic acidosis risk).

src.q: Combinations not recommended Alcohol Alcohol intoxication is associated with an increased risk of lactic acidosis

items.t: NSAIDs (including COX-2 inhibitors), ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists and diuretics (especially loop diuretics): may impair renal function and raise lactic acidosis risk; close monitoring of renal function is necessary.

src.q: e.g. NSAIDs, including selective cyclo-oxygenase (COX) II inhibitors, ACE inhibitors, angiotensin II receptor antagonists and diuretics, especially loop diuretics
When starting or using such products in combination with metformin, close monitoring of renal function is necessary.

items.t: Glucocorticoids, beta-2 agonists and diuretics raise blood glucose: inform the patient, monitor blood glucose more often (especially at the start), adjust the dose if needed. Thiazides, corticosteroids, thyroid products and sympathomimetics may reduce the effect of vildagliptin.

src.q: Glucocorticoids, beta-2-agonists, and diuretics have intrinsic hyperglycaemic activity.
The patient should be informed and more frequent blood glucose monitoring performed, especially at the beginning of treatment.
the hypoglycaemic effect of vildagliptin may be reduced by certain active substances, including thiazides, corticosteroids, thyroid products and sympathomimetics

items.t: ACE inhibitors: may lower blood glucose (adjust the antidiabetic dose if necessary); there may also be an increased risk of angioedema with vildagliptin.

src.q: Angiotensin converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors may decrease the blood glucose levels.
There may be an increased risk of angioedema in patients concomitantly taking ACE inhibitors.

items.t: OCT2/MATE inhibitors (e.g. ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir, cimetidine) could increase metformin exposure.

src.q: transporter-2 [OCT2] / multidrug and toxin extrusion [MATE] inhibitors such as ranolazine, vandetanib, dolutegravir and cimetidine) could increase systemic exposure to metformin

items.t: Vildagliptin: low interaction potential; no clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interactions with pioglitazone, metformin, glibenclamide, digoxin, warfarin, amlodipine, ramipril, valsartan or simvastatin.

src.q: Vildagliptin has a low potential for interactions with co-administered medicinal products.

items.t: Assess GFR before starting and at least annually; every 3 to 6 months in the elderly or if at risk of progression. Review lactic acidosis risk factors before starting if GFR < 60 mL/min.

src.q: A GFR should be assessed before initiation of treatment with metformin-containing products and at least annually thereafter.
Factors that may increase the risk of lactic acidosis (see section 4.4) should be reviewed before considering initiation of metformin in patients with GFR<60 ml/min.

items.t: GFR 60-89 mL/min: metformin maximum 3000 mg/day (dose reduction may be considered); vildagliptin no dose adjustment.

src.q: 60-89 Maximum daily dose is 3000 mg. Dose reduction may be considered in relation to declining renal function. No dose adjustment.

items.t: GFR 45-59 mL/min: metformin maximum 2000 mg/day (start at most half the maximum); vildagliptin maximum 50 mg/day.

src.q: 45-59 Maximum daily dose is 2000 mg. The starting dose is at most half of the maximum dose. Maximal daily dose is 50 mg.

items.t: GFR 30-44 mL/min: metformin maximum 1000 mg/day (start at most half the maximum). The SmPC table text gives no separate vildagliptin figure for this row; the fixed tablet twice daily exceeds these limits, so use the individual medicines if no suitable strength.

src.q: 30-44 Maximum daily dose is 1000 mg. The starting dose is at most half of the maximum dose.
If no adequate strength of Eucreas is available, individual monocomponents should be used instead of the fixed dose combination.

items.t: GFR < 30 mL/min: contraindicated.

src.q: Metformin is contraindicated in patients with GFR < 30 ml/min

items.t: Hepatic impairment: contraindicated (SmPC 4.3); includes pre-treatment ALT or AST > 3 x ULN.

src.q: Hepatic impairment (see sections 4.2, 4.4 and 4.8)

Eucreas should not be used in patients with hepatic impairment, including those with pre-treatment alanine aminotransferase (ALT) or aspartate aminotransferase (AST) > 3 times the upper limit of normal (ULN)

items.t: SmPC: no adequate human data; should not be used in pregnancy.

src.q: There are no adequate data from the use of Eucreas in pregnant women.
Eucreas should not be used during pregnancy.

items.t: BUMPS: type 2 diabetes in pregnancy should be treated with metformin, with insulin if needed; other antidiabetic medicines (including DPP-4 inhibitors) are avoided as a precaution.

src.q: Type 2 diabetes during pregnancy should be treated with metformin, as well as insulin if required. Other antidiabetic drugs should not be used.
As a precaution, they are avoided in pregnancy.

items.t: SmPC: contraindicated in breastfeeding (risk of neonatal hypoglycaemia from metformin; no human data for vildagliptin).

src.q: Due to both the potential risk of neonate hypoglycaemia related to metformin and the lack of human data with vildagliptin, Eucreas should not be used during breast-feeding
Breast-feeding (see section 4.6)

items.t: SPS: metformin (and insulin) are preferred choices in breastfeeding; there is limited or no published information on other antidiabetic medicines such as vildagliptin.

src.q: Insulin or metformin are the preferred choices during breastfeeding.
limited or no published information on the use of other antidiabetic (blood-glucose lowering) medicines during breastfeeding

src.q: No studies on the effect on human fertility have been conducted for Eucreas

items.t: Metformin stomach and bowel effects occur mostly at the start and usually settle; taking doses during or after meals helps.

src.q: Gastrointestinal adverse reactions occur most frequently during initiation of therapy and resolve spontaneously in most cases.

items.t: Lactic acidosis: acidotic breathlessness, abdominal pain, muscle cramps, weakness, low temperature, then coma. Stop and seek immediate medical attention.

src.q: Lactic acidosis is characterised by acidotic dyspnoea, abdominal pain, muscle cramps, asthenia and hypothermia followed by coma.
In case of suspected symptoms, the patient should stop taking metformin and seek immediate medical attention.

items.t: Hepatitis (uncommon) or liver dysfunction: stop if jaundice or signs of liver dysfunction; do not restart.

src.q: Hepatitis Uncommon
Patients who develop jaundice or other signs suggestive of liver dysfunction should discontinue Eucreas.

items.t: Pancreatitis (uncommon): stop if suspected; do not restart if confirmed.

if pancreatitis is suspected, the DPP-4 inhibitor and other potentially suspect medicines should be discontinued

items.t: GFR and liver function tests before starting.

items.t: GFR at least annually (every 3 to 6 months in the elderly or if at risk); liver function every 3 months in the first year, then periodically.

src.q: In patients at increased risk of further progression of renal impairment and in the elderly, renal function should be assessed more frequently, e.g. every 3-6 months.
Liver function should be monitored during treatment with Eucreas at three-month intervals during the first year and periodically thereafter.

items.t: Withdrawal recommended if AST or ALT ≥ 3 x ULN persists; stop if jaundice (do not restart). Withhold temporarily in dehydration, for surgery and for intravascular iodinated contrast.

src.q: Should an increase in AST or in ALT of 3x ULN or greater persist, withdrawal of Eucreas therapy is recommended.
Following withdrawal of treatment with Eucreas and LFT normalisation, treatment with Eucreas should not be re-initiated.
